results.title: Introducing Public Networks - Latitude.sh
highlights:
# Introducing Public Networks

September 10, 2026

Public Networks give you a dedicated public IP block you can control and use across your infrastructure.

That starts with network bonding: deploy servers with redundant network links so they stay connected if one link fails.

Keep your network configuration in place as your infrastructure changes.

- Redundant network links per server, stay connected if one fails.
- One IP block you control across your infrastructure, no reconfiguration as it changes.

Sizes /26 to /29 (59 to 3 servers), 5 IPs reserved per network, across 8 locations, 🇺🇸 🇬🇧 🇨🇦 🇦🇺 🇯🇵, starting at $32/month.

results.title: VM Apps: start with your stack, not an empty VM - Latitude.sh
highlights:
# VM Apps: start with your stack, not an empty VM

September 24, 2026

Deploy VMs with the software you need already installed and configured.

Choose from ready-made images for:

- AI Agents — Codex CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, and more
- Databases — PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, MariaDB
- Data Science — JupyterLab, Apache Kafka, and more

Pick an App, deploy your VM, and start working. New images are added regularly based on what customers actually run.

results.title: Object Storage, where you need it - Latitude.sh
highlights:
# Object Storage, where you need it

September 16, 2026

Create Object Storage buckets in supported locations, even where Latitude.sh bare metal isn't available.

This gives you more flexibility to place your data closer to your workloads, users, or preferred region without requiring compute infrastructure in the same location.

What’s new

- Create Object Storage buckets in new storage-only locations
- Choose from all supported locations directly when creating a bucket
- Storage availability is independent from bare metal availability
